use_when: A user-initiated action that resolves on the page it is on — submit, confirm, cancel, toggle a mode, open a dialog.
dont_use_when: Navigating to another URL: this renders a native `<button>` with no href, so it is invisible to a middle-click, a bookmark, and a crawler — use an anchor. Showing an arrow or glyph on its own: use IconSlot. A second Primary in the same view: demote it to Secondary, because Primary means the one thing this view wants you to do.
placement: Forms, cards, dialogs, toolbars, and the call to action closing a page section.
a11y: Native `<button>`, so it is in the tab order and Enter and Space activate it. Focus is visible on all three variants: `:focus-visible` replaces the shadow with `effect.focus-ring`. There are two independent ways to make it unavailable and they are OR-ed rather than overridden — `state="Disabled"` is the Figma axis, the native `disabled` attribute is the caller's runtime condition, so `disabled={isSubmitting}` really does disable and no value of `state` cancels it. `aria-busy` from a caller is honoured as given; `state="Loading"` supplies `aria-busy="true"` only when the caller has set none. Both verified on the deployed build. What it does not guarantee is that a Loading button is announced: Loading marks it natively disabled, so focus leaves it for `<body>` with nothing said, and `aria-busy` is not a live region — if the wait matters to a screen-reader user, announce it from somewhere that is. The trailing arrow is `aria-hidden`; the label carries the meaning. Target size is per-size and not equal: Md measures 36.2px tall from its tokens, which clears WCAG 2.5.8 AA at 24x24 and misses 2.5.5 AAA at 44x44; Lg measures 46.6px and clears both. Choose Lg where a 44px target is required. The loading spinner stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
